home.intro: A client-side suite for small-arms external ballistics. Everything runs in your browser — no data leaves the device.
home.trajectoryDesc: Bullets don't fly straight. Here's exactly how far off — drop, windage, velocity, time of flight, at any distance.
home.hitProbDesc: Hit probability against a target, accounting for wind, range-estimation and dispersion uncertainty.
home.truingSessionDesc: Plan a shooting session that separates muzzle velocity, drag and zero errors, then reports what it actually found.
home.arsenalDesc: Your rifles and bullets, with side-by-side comparison.
home.gunsDesc: Pick or manage the rifle and bullet used everywhere in the app.
home.privacyPolicy: We do not collect *any* data. Nothing is *ever* transmitted to the server.

home.contactText: Questions, feedback, or support requests go through the geladen.ch contact page — not this app.
home.thanksText: The people and projects that helped make this app possible.
home.troubleshootingText: Download information about this app's startup and caching state — useful when reporting a problem.
home.rebuildCacheText: If offline mode or update checks stop working, clear this app's cached files and service worker registration, then reload to rebuild them from scratch.

trajectory.title: Trajectory
trajectory.spinDriftUnavailable: Spin drift could not be calculated.
trajectory.dangerZoneChartHint: Each point along the horizontal axis is a zero distance; the shaded band shows how far before and after it the trajectory stays within the target.
trajectory.zeroRangeOverrideHint: Optional — leave blank to use the configured zero range unchanged. When set, this range is used only for this tool's calculations; it never changes the zero range configured in Guns.
trajectory.useOwnZeroHint: This cartridge is zeroed using another cartridge's ballistics (see Guns). Check this to use its own ballistics instead when solving the zero range override above.

bcEstimate.intro: Enter a near velocity and range, then either a far velocity or a measured time of flight to the far range, plus a drag model and atmosphere, to back out the ballistic coefficient that explains the observed change. If you have a choice, use residual velocity rather than time of flight — this is typically more precise.
bcEstimate.errorNearRangeExceedsFar: Near distance must be less than far distance.

bcTools.title: BC Tools
bcTools.intro: Calculate BC from known data, convert between different models, etc.
bcTools.invalidTof: Enter a valid time of flight (a positive number of seconds).

bcConversion.intro: Convert a ballistic coefficient from one standard drag model to another, at a single reference velocity. The conversion is exact at that velocity, and drifts the further your bullet's actual velocity strays from it — pick a velocity representative of the range band you care about.

bcToolsLabradar.intro: This tool only works with tracks from a Labradar v1 device (the big orange box). Upload a Labradar chronograph export (a .zip of track files) to fit a ballistic coefficient per shot, then average across the valid ones. Files that aren't real tracks — the device's own report or project files, or unrelated junk that ended up in the zip — are ignored automatically.
bcToolsLabradar.filterR2HintNone: Do not reject tracks based on fit quality.
bcToolsLabradar.filterR2HintHighNoise: Use if you run the radar in a particularly noisy environment (obstacles in or near the line of fire) and see too many valid measurements rejected.
bcToolsLabradar.filterSigmaHintNone: Disable if you are very sure of your data (single shooter, good conditions, radar well aligned to the target) — especially for small datasets of fewer than 10 shots.
bcToolsLabradar.filterSigmaHintConservative: Recommended default — rejects tracks whose BC is more than 2× the standard deviation from the mean, e.g. a shot picked up from a nearby lane.
bcToolsLabradar.filterSigmaHintAggressive: Rejects more aggressively — useful on a busy range with similar calibers nearby, or without realigning between targets. May also discard some valid data, reducing accuracy.
bcToolsLabradar.denoiseHint: Leave at 0.990 (Normal), unless you are operating in a very noisy environment and are losing too many valid data points.
bcToolsLabradar.chartEmptyHint: Select a track below to see its velocity-vs-time curve.
bcToolsLabradar.ci95Title: 95% confidence interval of the averaged BC, as a percentage of that BC. Wider with fewer shots or more shot-to-shot spread.
bcToolsLabradar.emptyBatchError: No track files were found in that zip.

cdMachCurve.title: Cd–Mach Curve
cdMachCurve.intro: Paste a distance/velocity table (e.g. Doppler radar or multi-chronograph readings) to back out this bullet's own drag curve, segment by segment.
cdMachCurve.tableInstructions: One pair per line: distance, then velocity, separated by tab, space or semicolon. Decimal point or comma both work.
cdMachCurve.tableRecommendationHint: Aim for consecutive velocities at least ~20 m/s (~65 fps) apart — narrower segments are extended automatically, but tightly bunched readings still add more rounding noise than real resolution. If the table's velocities never drop well below Mach 1.0 (~340 m/s / ~1125 fps), it stays entirely supersonic and won't capture any transonic behavior — a standard G1/G7 model with a BC estimated over Mach 2.5–1.5 (~850 m/s / ~2790 fps down to ~510 m/s / ~1675 fps) will likely serve you better (see BC Tools).
cdMachCurve.tableErrorTooFewRows: Enter at least 3 distance/velocity pairs, one per line.
cdMachCurve.tableErrorBadLine: Line {{line}}: expected a distance and a velocity, separated by tab, space or semicolon.
cdMachCurve.errorMassCaliberRequired: Enter the bullet's mass and caliber first.
cdMachCurve.skippedSegmentsWarning: {{count}} segment(s) skipped (see below) — the rest of the table is unaffected.
cdMachCurve.skipReasonNonDecreasingVelocity: velocity didn't decrease between these two rows
cdMachCurve.skipReasonNotConverged: solver didn't converge for this segment
cdMachCurve.skipReasonNonPositiveCd: solver hit a non-physical drag coefficient for this segment

multiBc.intro: Turn 2-5 manufacturer-published BC values, each valid over its own speed band, into a bullet-specific Cd-Mach curve — drag the segment borders on the chart, or type them into the table below it.
multiBc.massCaliberHint: Mass and caliber both directly affect the resulting curve and the optimal BC values below — enter them accurately.
multiBc.chartHint: Click the chart to add a segment border, drag a border to move it, click × on a border to remove it.
multiBc.maxSegmentsHint: A maximum of {{max}} segments is supported.
multiBc.errorFromExceedsTo: This value must be strictly between its own segment's neighboring borders.
multiBc.optimalBcHint: A single BC per model that best approximates this bullet's own supersonic behavior, computed between Mach {{startMach}} (muzzle) and Mach {{endMach}} (the beginning of the transonic band), in standard sea-level atmosphere.
multiBc.optimalBcUnreachable: No BC value for this model reproduces this bullet's supersonic behavior within the usual range.

hitProbability.title: Hit Probability
hitProbability.intro: Probability of hitting a target for a chosen firing scenario, given your rifle and load, accounting for your own precision and the conditions of the shot.
hitProbability.syncHint: Same selection as on the Trajectory page — picking a rifle or bullet here updates it there too.
hitProbability.simplifiedHint: This value represents the combined precision of rifle, cartridge, and shooter in your typical shooting position.
hitProbability.battleZeroToggleLabel: Battle zero (rifle zeroed at a different range)
hitProbability.contributionHeadingSighting: Contribution to total error - sighting shot
hitProbability.contributionHeadingCorrected: Contribution to total error - corrected shot
hitProbability.thisRigMuzzleVelocitySDHint: This cartridge specifies its own muzzle velocity consistency (SD) — pick "This rig's" above to use it.
hitProbability.thisRigPrecisionHint: This cartridge specifies its own rifle precision — see "This rig's" below.

rangeSolver.rangeCardNoTargetsHint: This location has no targets yet — add some from the Locations manager.
rangeSolver.rangeCardNoPhotoHint: Add a photo to this location to pick targets visually here.

rangeSolverLocations.title: Locations & Targets
rangeSolverLocations.intro: Save a shooting location's targets once, then pick them straight from the Target tab on later visits — wind and atmosphere are never part of this, only range, angle and where each target is.
rangeSolverLocations.noLocationOption: No location — single target, manual entry
rangeSolverLocations.notPlacedBadgeTitle: Not yet placed on the location photo
rangeSolverLocations.altitudeHint: Optional. If set, making this location active fills in the Atmosphere tab with the standard atmosphere at this altitude and 50% humidity — but only if you haven't already changed atmosphere values yourself this session.
rangeSolverLocations.photoHint: Attach a photo taken from the shooting position to quickly pick a target visually, instead of a name list.
rangeSolverLocations.cropHint: Drag the corners to crop the photo, or leave them at the edges to use the whole photo.
rangeSolverLocations.photoProcessingError: Could not process that photo. Please try a different file.
rangeSolverLocations.duplicateNameWarning: A location with this name already exists — saving will overwrite it.
rangeSolverLocations.duplicateTargetNameWarning: Another target at this location already has this name.
rangeSolverLocations.targetNameHint: Optional — leave blank to use "Target 1", "Target 2", etc.
rangeSolverLocations.pinFieldHint: Tap the photo to place this target's pin, drag it to fine-tune, pinch to zoom, drag empty space to pan.
rangeSolverLocations.importFileErrorInvalidFormat: That file isn't a recognized Locations library export.
rangeSolverLocations.photoOverlayHint: Tap a target to select it.

riflePrecision.title: Rifle Precision Calculator
riflePrecision.intro: Photograph a paper target, mark the point of aim and every bullet hole, and get real precision numbers — extreme spread, group centroid, and pooled statistics once you're ready — across as many targets and groups as you like.
riflePrecision.unusableBadgeTitle: Missing calibration, point of aim, or an impact — this target cannot be analyzed
riflePrecision.noArsenalCartridgesHint: You don't have any Arsenal cartridges yet — add a rifle and cartridge first.
riflePrecision.cropHint: Drag the corners to crop the photo, or leave them at the edges to use the whole photo.
riflePrecision.photoProcessingError: Could not process that photo. Please try a different file.
riflePrecision.calibrationHint1: Tap the photo at the first calibration point — one end of a ruler or a known-length feature on the target.
riflePrecision.calibrationHint2: Tap the photo at the second calibration point, then enter the real-world distance between the two points.
riflePrecision.poaHint: Tap the photo to place this group's point of aim.
riflePrecision.shotHint: Tap the photo to record each bullet hole — keep tapping to add more.
riflePrecision.deleteImpactHint: Tap the impact you want to remove, or Cancel to keep it.
riflePrecision.idleHint: Pick a group below to keep adding shots to it, or add a new group.
riflePrecision.noShotsToAnalyzeHint: There is nothing to analyse yet. Mark some shots first.
riflePrecision.impactsToScaleHint: Draws each impact at the bullet's true bore diameter instead of a fixed marker size. Switch off for visual clarity, if there is too much overlap between the impacts (precise rifle at short distance).
riflePrecision.duplicateNameWarning: An entry with this name already exists in your Rifle Precision library — saving will overwrite it.
riflePrecision.importFileErrorInvalidFormat: That file doesn't look like a Rifle Precision export.
riflePrecision.r50Description: Circular error probable, the radius of a circle where 50% of impacts are expected to fall
riflePrecision.r95Description: The radius of a circle where 95% of impacts are expected to fall
riflePrecision.r99Description: The radius of a circle where 99% of impacts are expected to fall

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: Choose a preferred unit for each kind of measurement — mix metric and imperial freely. These apply everywhere that measurement appears across the tools and are remembered on this device.
settings.zeroForSpinDriftLabel: Account for spin drift when zeroing
settings.showTroubleshootingLabel: Show Troubleshooting pane on Home page
settings.rangeSolverLabelVisibilityDeclutter: Hide near pointer, show closest target
settings.rangeSolverLabelVisibilityTap: Hide labels, tap to show, tap again to select
settings.rangeSolverLabelVisibilityHint: Hiding labels near the pointer has no effect on devices that don't have a mouse.
settings.dragModelsHint: Hide standard drag models you don't use, to declutter the drag-model picker. A hidden model stays available wherever it's already selected — hiding it never changes an existing choice.
settings.csvSeparatorHint: Should be different from each other, or spreadsheet software may not read the file correctly.

changeHistory.heading: Change History
changeHistory.intro: A local safety net for your Arsenal, Locations, and Rifle Precision libraries — recent edits and deletions can be reverted here, whether made on this device or merged in from another.

backupSync.heading: Backup & Sync
backupSync.experimentalWarning: Experimental — use at your own risk. Back up all your libraries before continuing.
backupSync.confirmIntro: This is experimental. Before continuing, back up your libraries with the existing export options:
backupSync.deviceNameHint: Give this device a name you'll recognize — especially important if you have more than one similar device.
backupSync.folderHint: Pick a folder that your cloud provider (iCloud Drive, OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, etc.) already keeps in sync across your devices — this app doesn't talk to any cloud service itself, it just reads and writes a small backup file there.
backupSync.folderChosen: Currently synchronizing to the selected folder.
backupSync.modeHint: Manually only syncs when you press Sync Now. Switch to Automatically to also sync every few minutes and whenever you return to this tab.
backupSync.manualModeHint: This browser can't keep a folder connected, so Sync picks your synced folder each time: it reads every device's backup file (and any photos alongside it) from that folder, merges them in, then downloads your own updated backup — save that back into the same folder.
backupSync.manualModeWarning: Do not change the proposed file name. Overwrite the existing file if prompted.
backupSync.iosModeHint: This device can't keep a folder connected, so Sync picks one or more backup files from your synced folder in the Files app, merges them in, then shares your own updated backup back out — choose "Save to Files" to put it in the same folder.
backupSync.iosModeWarning: Do not change the proposed file name. If Files asks, choose Replace, not Keep Both.
backupSync.manualSyncSummary: Merged {{count}} device(s). Your own updated backup was just exported.
backupSync.importErrorInvalidFormat: That doesn't look like a backup file from this app.
backupSync.photoWarning: Some photos from {{devices}} haven't finished syncing yet — retrying automatically.
backupSync.clockSkewWarning: {{devices}}'s clock appears to be wrong (either running ahead, or it jumped backward since its last sync). Merges involving it may resolve incorrectly until it's corrected.
backupSync.iphoneSyncHint: Makes it compatible with iPhones, but makes it heavy and inefficient for everybody else.

review.reasonUnresolvableTimestamp: Reason: one side's timestamp couldn't be read, so this can't be resolved automatically.
review.reasonDiverged: Reason: both sides were edited at the exact same moment, with different content.

backupSync.verboseLoggingHint: Prints live sync activity to the browser's console.
backupSync.clearLogHint: Empties the live trace and the stored sync history that the diagnostics download includes.

cleanup.runNowHint: Reconciles stored history and removes photo files in the sync folder that no device uses any more.
cleanup.reportHistory: Removed {{count}} change-history entries beyond the limit.

devices.heading: Devices
devices.noBackup: no backup file in the folder
devices.pickHint: Choose the device you want to delete. You will be asked to confirm.
devices.blockedConflicts: {{device}} has {{count}} unresolved conflicts. Resolve them before deleting this device, so nothing it holds is lost.
devices.blockedPhotos: Photos from {{device}} are still arriving. Wait until syncing has caught up before deleting it.
devices.blockedNotMerged: {{device}} has not been synced on this device yet. Sync first, so nothing it holds is lost.
devices.confirmBody: Its backup file is removed from the sync folder, and it disappears from the device list on all your devices. Photos only it used are cleared later.
devices.confirmBodyNoFolder: This browser cannot delete files in the sync folder, so its backup file stays there for now and every device ignores it. Sync afterwards to pass the deletion on: it disappears from the device list on all your devices, and a Chrome or Edge device removes the file the next time it syncs.
devices.confirmMerged: Everything it held has already been merged here.
devices.confirmRejoins: Do this only for devices that are out of circulation. If that computer is still live, it will re-join as soon as it syncs the next time.
devices.confirmRecent: This device was still syncing on {{when}}, so it is probably in use.

gate.needsArsenal: This tool needs an Arsenal rifle and cartridge — it writes its result back to a cartridge record, and there's nothing to write to otherwise.
gate.needsLocation: This tool plans against your saved distances — pick an active location with at least one target first.

prepare.startBlockedHint: Confirm your distances and angles below ("All checked, all good") before starting.
prepare.optimalHeading: The best distances for this rifle
prepare.nearLine: Near target: your zero range ({{zero}}) works well, and anything out to about {{limit}} works almost as well.
prepare.farLine: Far target: aim for about {{optimum}} — anywhere from {{low}} out to {{high}} still gives a convincing result. Beyond {{high}} the bullet is no longer comfortably supersonic, which this session does not model.
prepare.farLineNoBand: Far target: as far as possible, ideally about {{optimum}} and no farther than {{high}} — no supersonic distance reaches a convincing result with this load, so every metre helps.
prepare.altitudeLine: Thinner air moves the far limit out: at {{alt}} altitude ({{air}}) it would be about {{to}} instead of {{from}} — {{pct}}% farther.
prepare.invalidityLine: Under about {{floor}}, this load's drag signal is smaller than what any number of rounds can resolve. If that is the longest target your range has, this session can still true your come-ups there, but it cannot produce a BC correction — more rounds will not change that.
prepare.invalidityNone: No supersonic distance escapes the "come-up correction only" grade for this load, whatever the round count — this session can true your come-ups, not your BC.
prepare.farCheckDistance: The precision of this session's result depends strongly on the distance to your far target ({{far}}), and a wrong distance can be very hard to catch from the shots alone. Before you start, measure it again with your rangefinder — several reads, watching for a beam that catches something in front of the target. Skipping this is the most costly mistake in a session: a far distance {{err}} out typically leaves the result about {{cost}} off there (about {{length}} at {{at}}), and the tool will not flag it, it will blame your bullet's BC instead.
prepare.farCheckDistanceAngle: The precision of this session's result depends strongly on the distance and angle of your far target ({{far}}), and a wrong distance or an unrecorded slope can be very hard to catch from the shots alone. Before you start, measure both again — the distance with your rangefinder (several reads, watching for a beam that catches something in front of the target) and the angle with a clinometer. Skipping this is the most costly mistake in a session: a far distance {{err}} out typically leaves the result about {{cost}} off there (about {{length}} at {{at}}), and the tool will not flag it, it will blame your bullet's BC instead.
prepare.roundBudgetLabel: Rounds for the session (the total, safety steps included)
prepare.startBlockedConditions: Confirm today's atmospheric conditions above before starting.

homework.heading: Homework — none of it required, all of it cheap
homework.zeroVerified: Zero re-verified on the day, as a measured group
homework.trackTested: Scope click value confirmed with a tall-target (or ruler) test
homework.mvAverageChecked: Today's actual muzzle velocity average verified — separately from its SD
homework.oneLot: One ammunition lot for the whole session
homework.coldBoreHandled: Cold-bore shot decided in advance (discarded, or recorded separately)
homework.windConfidenceLabel: How confident are you calling the wind?
homework.intro: Nothing below is mandatory. But getting it right beforehand removes sources of uncertainty this session would otherwise have to absorb, and makes the result far more conclusive.
homework.sightHeightMeasured: Sight height physically measured (bore axis to scope axis), not assumed
homework.zeroHint: Confirm nothing has shifted since the zero was last verified. On a busy range the near target's in-session read of your zero is usually a rough glance, so a solid, freshly verified zero is doing real work here.
homework.trackHint: A tall-target test works; so does a ruler at a short known distance — dial a known number of clicks between two shots and measure the shift ({{rule}}).
homework.r50Missing: No dispersion on record for this cartridge — measure it with the Rifle Precision tool and enter the result into the cartridge's Arsenal record.
homework.mvSdShotsLabel: Shots this SD was measured from (only if you typed it in yourself)
homework.mvSdHint: To measure it: chronograph at least 10 shots of this exact load (20 is better) and compute the sample SD — divide the sum of squared deviations by N − 1, not N — then enter it into the cartridge record.
homework.mvAverageHint: The single most important item here. Enter the measured average as the cartridge's muzzle velocity, and the ammunition's own temperature at that moment (not the air's) as its reference temperature, so the app can correct for today's temperature.
homework.ruleMrad: 1 mm per metre of distance is 1 mrad
homework.ruleMoaImperial: about 1 inch per 100 yards is 1 MOA
homework.ruleMoaMetric: about 2.9 cm per 100 m is 1 MOA

equipment.heading: Equipment for today
equipment.rangefinderMandatory: Laser rangefinder — mandatory, and it must reliably reach your far target.
equipment.angleMeterMandatory: A way to measure the inclination angle (clinometer, or a rangefinder that shows it directly) — mandatory unless the range is flat. A rangefinder that only shows an angle-compensated distance does not qualify.
equipment.weatherMeterMandatory: Pocket weather meter — mandatory. Use station pressure, never a sea-level-reduced (QNH) reading.
equipment.chronographHint: Only a radar/Doppler or muzzle-mounted unit that reports every shot as you go — an optical trap set up away from the targets doesn't count here. Without one, the muzzle-velocity homework above matters even more.
equipment.backdropHint: Total height, with the target's point of aim assumed centered in it. We'll never ask you to shoot at a distance where a bad guess could put the impact outside this, up or down. Use at least {{two}}.
equipment.backdropSmall: That is small. Use at least {{two}} ({{one}} up and {{one}} down): with a {{one}} backdrop about a third of sessions lose an impact off it, with {{two}} a few in a hundred.

location.heading: Double-check your distances and angles before we plan around them
location.flatRangeLabel: This range is flat — no line-of-sight angle anywhere beyond 5°
location.flatRangeHint: Turns off angle inputs and inclination checks for this session.
location.allCheckedRequiredHint: Required — confirm you've re-checked every distance and angle above before this session plans around them.
location.allCheckedConfirmedHint: Confirmed for this session. Re-press this if you edit anything above.
location.naturalTargetPrompt: A rock, a backdrop, anything you can range or pace off — look for something near {{target}}, anywhere from {{low}} to {{high}} still gives a convincing result.
location.recheckInstructions: For each target, re-measure the distance with your laser rangefinder, and take a few reads, not one. A read shorter than you expect is usually the beam catching a branch, a fence post or the front lip of the berm. If your reads disagree, or the number differs from what's saved, fix it below.
location.recheckAngleInstructions: If you have a recorded angle to a target, check it the same way — a repeat clinometer reading — before trusting it. Enter it with its sign — uphill positive, downhill negative — because the wrong sign leaves a small but real error on a long, steep shot.
location.naturalTargetQuestion: Do you have other distances available today — a rock, a backdrop, anything you can range or pace off that isn't one of your saved targets?
location.naturalAnsweredNo: Planning with your saved targets only.
location.naturalSessionOnly: Distances added here are for this session only — they are never written to the location.

rangeGrading.heading: Is this range long enough?
rangeGrading.noUsableDistance: None of your saved targets are usable for this rifle's current ballistic profile — the supersonic ceiling here is only {{ceiling}}. Double-check the cartridge's BC and drag model before assuming the range itself is the problem.
rangeGrading.gradeA: Grade A: a real BC correction.
rangeGrading.gradeB: Grade B: a BC correction with a wide band.
rangeGrading.gradeC: Grade C: little more than the published BC.
rangeGrading.gradeD: Grade D: a come-up correction for these ranges only — no BC conclusion.
rangeGrading.noChronoWarning: No chronograph, no BC correction — this session will still true your come-ups and zero.
rangeGrading.chronoLeverHint: The far target's distance and a chronograph both matter far more than round count alone.
rangeGrading.targetAtXHelps: A target at {{x}} would bring this to grade {{grade}}.
rangeGrading.excludedSubsonic: Not used: {{ranges}} — beyond {{ceiling}} the bullet is no longer comfortably supersonic, and its transonic behaviour is not modelled by this session.
rangeGrading.budgetTooSmall: {{n}} rounds are too few to plan a session — at least one per distance is needed.
rangeGrading.zeroDragOverlap: Overlap between zero and drag in this plan: correlation {{corr}} (0 = cleanly separated, 1 = inseparable).
rangeGrading.walkOut: The plan already includes {{steps}} intermediate steps ({{ranges}}) that only check it is safe to go farther — they are inside the {{planned}} rounds, not on top.
rangeGrading.budgetKnee: About {{n}} rounds is where extra rounds start to pay much less. The rows below show what ten and twenty more would buy.
rangeGrading.budgetFlat: More rounds hardly help here: even {{n}} rounds leave the drag scale at ±{{sd}}% (grade {{letter}}). What limits it is the homework and the distances — see the advice above.
rangeGrading.budgetMinimum: These are minimum numbers: they count only the rounds whose impact you can see. A round the spotter cannot see (off the backdrop, or lost) does not count — bring more than the table says.
rangeGrading.walkOutNone: No intermediate steps expected on the way to the far target.
rangeGrading.walkOutGap: The shot ladder cannot step safely from {{last}} to {{far}} with the distances available — it steps at most four times a validated distance, or further only when the predicted miss stays on the backdrop. Add a distance between {{last}} and {{max}} (a natural target counts).

shoot.resolvedLabel: I could clearly make out individual shots on this target
shoot.cantSeeImpactButton: I can't see where it hit
shoot.liveDisclaimer: Provisional — this can and will change as more groups come in.
shoot.missedImpactCount: Shots that couldn't be located on the backdrop: {{n}}
shoot.addDistanceButton: Add this distance for the session
shoot.liveNotYet: {{param}}: not determined yet — the shots so far haven't moved it off the starting assumption.
shoot.plannedStep: A planned target — rounds planned here: {{shots}}.
shoot.rungStep: An intermediate step, only to make sure the next jump is safe — one round is enough.
shoot.chronoPlaceholder: e.g. {{example}} (a - is a shot the chronograph missed)
shoot.backdropLabel: Backdrop height ({{unit}}, target centred in it)
shoot.ladderDone: The ladder is complete — every planned distance has been shot. Finish and conclude when you're ready.
shoot.ladderStuck: No further step is safe with what is known so far, and the planned far target ({{far}}) was not reached — the farthest validated distance is {{farthest}}. Conclude on what was shot, or add an intermediate distance.
shoot.missRetreat: Couldn't spot that one? That's useful information on its own — let's step back in and check from {{range}} instead.
shoot.missNoRetreat: Couldn't spot that one? That's useful information on its own — the ladder will not go that far again until another group has been recorded, and then only once more, with the elevation shown for it.
shoot.sdOverride: Today's chronograph spread ({{today}} over {{n}} shots) differs significantly from the recorded {{recorded}} — this session now uses today's figure.
shoot.sdSessionOnly: Used for this session only; the cartridge record is unchanged.
shoot.nextShotFromFit: From the fit so far: the muzzle velocity, drag and zero it has learned are folded in, in the air and wind of that shot. Bands are 95%.
shoot.nextShotFromApp: Nothing is recorded yet, so this is the app's own dope for these conditions.
shoot.nextShotDialFull: Dial this in full, shoot, and record what you dialed. The come-up you enter is the whole dial, not a correction on top of this number. Windage is only predicted from the wind you called; the tool learns nothing from sideways impacts.
shoot.ladderStuckCap: The next planned distance ({{far}}) is more than four times the farthest distance shot so far ({{farthest}}), and the ladder will not jump that far. A distance between {{low}} and {{high}} would let it go on.
shoot.ladderStuckBackdrop: The backdrop is too small for {{far}}: with what is known so far the impact could miss it. A taller backdrop, or a nearer distance, would let the ladder go on.
shoot.ladderStuckMisses: Impacts you could not see are most often a wrong drag model or BC. Check first that the cartridge's BC and its drag model (G1 or G7) match their published source. Then the zero, the muzzle velocity, and the pressure entered (a sea-level-reduced QNH value at altitude), which the tool cannot tell apart from these.
shoot.intermediateQuestion: Is there another target between those distances, or any natural target you can use (a rock, a post)? Enter its distance.
shoot.noIntermediateAnswer: Then the ladder cannot go on from here. You can conclude on what was shot. If an impact was missed, shooting another group at a distance that has landed gives the missed distance one more try, at the elevation shown for it.
shoot.repeatStep: An extra group at a distance that has already landed, to update the fit before the missed distance is tried once more. Three rounds.
shoot.firstRungWarning: The first shot, at {{range}}, may leave the backdrop: nothing has been shot yet, so the tool cannot be sure where it lands (about ± {{miss}} expected, against a backdrop {{backdrop}} tall), and there is nothing nearer to fall back on. A nearer distance is safer; the zero range is the natural one.

conclusion.heading: Conclusion
conclusion.noData: No groups were recorded this session.
conclusion.missedImpactCount: Shots that couldn't be located on the backdrop this session: {{n}}
conclusion.implausibleWarning: This result is far outside anything a BC or MV measurement error would normally produce — check the cartridge's BC value and drag model before trusting it.
conclusion.planFarNotReached: The planned far target ({{planned}}) was not reached — the farthest distance shot is {{farthest}}, and everything below is graded on what was actually shot.
conclusion.pMaterial: Probability this matters at your longest distance: {{p}}
conclusion.case1NothingMaterial: Nothing material found — the session validates your current setup. That is a real result.
conclusion.notDetermined: Not determined by this session, so neither cleared nor confirmed: {{causes}}.
conclusion.notDeterminedClick: The click value is settled by a tall-target (or ruler) test on its own, not by shooting.
conclusion.case1NothingMaterialOpen: Nothing material found among the causes this session could determine. That is a real result.
conclusion.case2Dial: A come-up correction for exactly the distances shot (grade {{grade}} — no BC conclusion from this session):
conclusion.dialMore: at {{range}}: dial {{mrad}} ({{clicks}} clicks) more than predicted
conclusion.dialLess: at {{range}}: dial {{mrad}} ({{clicks}} clicks) less than predicted
conclusion.case3OfferBc: Save this to {{cartridge}}? Its BC gain factor goes from {{from}} to {{to}} — an effective {{model}} BC of {{newBc}} instead of {{oldBc}}.
conclusion.case3OfferCd: Save this to {{cartridge}}? Its BC gain factor goes from {{from}} to {{to}} — its Cd table scaled to {{pct}}% {{direction}}.
conclusion.savedLabel: Saved — the cartridge's BC gain factor is now {{factor}}.
conclusion.bcSessionOnlyLabel: Kept for this session only — the cartridge was not changed.
conclusion.case4ActionUp: Your impacts sit low: move your zero {{clicks}} clicks up.
conclusion.case4ActionDown: Your impacts sit high: move your zero {{clicks}} clicks down.
conclusion.case5Tracking: A scope-tracking finding: the scope under-delivers by {{size}} per click — get the scope checked or re-measure its click value. This is hardware, not a ballistic correction.
conclusion.measuredV0: Measured muzzle velocity differs from the cartridge's value by {{size}} — update the cartridge's muzzle velocity (a measurement, not a fitted number).
conclusion.case6Joint: {{causes}}: together they shift your come-up at {{rMax}} by {{value}} ± {{size}}, but this session cannot say which of them it is.
conclusion.case6ActionChrono: A chronograph separates these two — bring one next time.
conclusion.case6ActionSeparate: Checking one of these independently before the next session would separate them.
conclusion.case8Unresolved: {{param}}: this session did not determine it ({{size}} is mostly your starting assumption) — a different session design would be needed.
conclusion.case8NoChrono: {{param}}: {{size}}, but without at least 5 chronograph readings this session cannot tell a BC error from a muzzle-velocity error, so no BC correction is offered.
conclusion.case8Grade: {{param}}: {{size}} — at grade {{grade}} the band is too wide to write as a BC correction. A farther target or a chronograph would sharpen it.
conclusion.case8Possible: {{param}}: {{size}} is possible, but not yet clear — this session's data is too thin to call it a correction. Don't change anything on this alone; a second look (more rounds, or a check on the day) would settle it.
conclusion.case8Overlap: {{a}} and {{b}} overlap somewhat (correlation {{corr}}) — more rounds at the near target next time would sharpen the distinction.
conclusion.newSessionConfirm: Tap again to discard this session and start over
conclusion.bcAssumesAir: This correction assumes the conditions used ({{summary}}) were right. A wrong temperature or pressure is taken up by the drag term, so check them before saving it.
conclusion.measuredV0Advice: To settle it, chronograph about {{n}} rounds in one string (your shot-to-shot spread of {{sd}} then puts the average within about ±{{tol}}), ideally at today's temperature, and enter the average in the cartridge. If the difference follows the temperature, the cartridge's temperature sensitivity may be off too: repeat on a day with a different temperature.
conclusion.homeworkAssumed: You ticked as done: {{items}}. The stated uncertainties and the grade take every one of them as really done; if one was optimistic, the true uncertainty is larger than shown (in tests, a check ticked but not done left the truth outside the stated band about half the time). Re-check it on a target before trusting the numbers.

choice.sessionOnly: Use for this truing session only

advice.heading: What would help
advice.nearRoundsFree: {{n}} more rounds at the near target: drag {{fromSd}} → {{toSd}}, zero/drag overlap {{fromCorr}} → {{toCorr}} — better on both counts.
advice.nearRoundsShift: If you can't bring more: moving {{n}} rounds from the far target to the near one: drag {{fromSd}} → {{toSd}}, zero/drag overlap {{fromCorr}} → {{toCorr}} — a trade, not a free gain.
advice.tallTarget: Check your click value (tall-target or ruler test): {{from}} → {{to}}.

flag.distanceOrAngle: The target at {{range}} looks wrong ({{p}}): either its distance or an unrecorded slope — from the shots alone the two can't be told apart.
flag.distance: The distance to the target at {{range}} looks wrong ({{p}}).
flag.screened: (An estimate from the quick check — this target was not in the detailed comparison.)

recheck.promptWithAngle: Re-range the target at {{range}} — and put a clinometer on it while you're there.
recheck.noAngleTool: I have no way to measure the angle
recheck.noAngleCaveat: Without an angle we can't separate a wrong distance from a slope here; both stay on the table.
recheck.needValues: Enter the distance, and the angle unless you have no way to measure it.

conditions.heading: Conditions at the rifle
conditions.intro: Enter the weather where you are shooting, now. Use station pressure (what a barometer at the rifle reads), never a sea-level-reduced (QNH) value from a phone or a weather app. Temperature to about 3 °C, measured at the rifle; humidity matters little, leave it if you don't know it. The plan and every fit use these values, and a BC correction assumes them right: a wrong temperature or pressure is taken up by the drag term.
conditions.confirmLabel: These are today's conditions at the rifle
conditions.pressureQnh: {{entered}} is much higher than the air at {{altitude}} normally is (about {{expected}}). It looks like a sea-level-reduced (QNH) reading. Enter the station pressure your barometer shows at the rifle, or the tool will blame your bullet's BC for the difference.
conditions.pressureLow: {{entered}} is much lower than the air at {{altitude}} normally is (about {{expected}}). Check the pressure and the location's altitude.
conditions.groupChanged: The weather at this target has changed since the start
conditions.groupChangedAgain: The weather has changed again since the last group
conditions.groupSameAsLast: Otherwise this group counts as shot in: {{summary}}
conditions.changedALot: The weather is now quite different from the start, and the plan was made for the start. The fit uses each group's own weather, but rounds planned for the old air may no longer be the best ones. Shoot the rest of the session quickly.
conditions.zeroFromArsenal: The zero is taken to have been made in the cartridge's zero atmosphere (from Arsenal): {{summary}}.
conditions.zeroFromConditions: The zero is taken to have been made once, in the air above. If it was made in other air (another day or altitude), set the cartridge's zero atmosphere in Arsenal; it matters mostly for a zero of {{long}} or more.

guns.customIntro: Pick a built-in rifle, one of your own Arsenal rifles, or enter everything by hand. This configuration is shared by every tool that needs a specific rifle and bullet.

arsenal.title: Arsenal
arsenal.intro: Your own rifles and bullets, stored on this device. They show up alongside the built-in library everywhere a rifle or bullet can be picked, marked with a leading "*".
arsenal.manualRifleActiveMessage: The currently selected rifle is manually defined and is not listed in your Arsenal.
arsenal.noCartridgesWarning: This rifle has no cartridges defined. This configuration is unusable and will not be set active.
arsenal.unusableBadgeTitle: No cartridges defined — this rifle cannot be made active
arsenal.zeroDonorBadgeTitle: This cartridge's own zero elevation is borrowed by one or more other cartridges on this rifle
arsenal.zeroRecipientBadgeTitle: Zeroed with {{name}} — its elevation, not this cartridge's own, is used to calculate the zero
arsenal.comparisonFullHint: Remove a configuration from comparison first
arsenal.noBullets: No bullets in your Arsenal yet.
arsenal.noBulletsFiltered: No bullets match the current filter.
arsenal.noRifles: No rifles in your Arsenal yet.
arsenal.noRiflesFiltered: No rifles match the current filter.
arsenal.bulletLengthHint: Optional — used to estimate bullet stability (Miller's formula) and spin drift (Litz's formula). Leave blank if unknown.
arsenal.cdTableInstructions:
One row per line: Mach number, a space, then the drag coefficient (Cd) at that Mach. At least 2 rows, with Mach strictly increasing down the list.
Example:
0.85 0.230
0.95 0.310
1.00 0.380
1.20 0.360
arsenal.cdTableErrorTooFewRows: Enter at least 2 rows (Mach and Cd, one pair per line).
arsenal.cdTableErrorBadLine: Line {{line}}: expected two numbers (Mach and Cd) separated by a space.
arsenal.cdTableErrorBadValue: Line {{line}}: Mach must be 0 or greater and Cd must be greater than 0.
arsenal.cdTableErrorNotIncreasing: Line {{line}}: Mach values must increase strictly from one row to the next.
arsenal.cdTableErrorOutOfRange: Line {{line}}: Cd must be between 0.05 and 3.0.
arsenal.riflingTwistHint: Optional — used to estimate bullet stability (Miller's formula) and spin drift (Litz's formula). Leave blank if unknown.
arsenal.cartridgeBulletHint: Select an existing bullet from your Arsenal, or add a new one.
arsenal.cartridgeCaliberLockedHint: Locked to this rifle's existing caliber (set by its other cartridges).
arsenal.cartridgeBulletCopyNotice: This is a built-in bullet — saving this cartridge will add a copy of it to your bullet library, and the cartridge will refer to that copy.
arsenal.cartridgeBulletCopyOverwriteWarning: A bullet named "{{name}}" already exists in your library — saving will overwrite it.
arsenal.hitProbabilityOnlyHint: Optional — used only by the Hit Probability tool.
arsenal.bcGainFactorHint: 1.00 = as published. 1.05 = behaves as if the BC were 5% higher (less drag, flatter). Written by the Truing Session tool, or editable here directly.
arsenal.bcGainFactorWarning: This is far outside a typical BC error; check the bullet's drag model and BC against its published source.
arsenal.bcGainFactorReadoutCdTableLess: Cd table scaled to {{pct}}% less drag
arsenal.bcGainFactorReadoutCdTableMore: Cd table scaled to {{pct}}% more drag
arsenal.cartridgeZeroedWithHint: Optional — if this rifle was physically zeroed while shooting a different cartridge, pick it here. Trajectory, Range Solver, and Arsenal's comparison chart will then calculate this cartridge's elevation as if it shared that cartridge's own zero, instead of solving its own. Hit Probability always uses this cartridge's own zero.
arsenal.cartridgeZeroedWithDisabledHint: Not available — one or more other cartridges on this rifle are already zeroed with this one.
arsenal.cartridgeZeroAtmosphereHint: Optional — the temperature, pressure and humidity at which this cartridge's zero was set. Trajectory and Range Solver then solve the zero elevation angle in this air. (They always solve it on the level, in calm air, whatever line-of-sight angle or wind is set.) Cartridges zeroed with this one use it too.
arsenal.cartridgePrecisionCheckboxLabel: Specify rifle precision for this cartridge
arsenal.cartridgePrecisionHint: Be honest. Use average, not best. Refer to the Rifle Precision tool for meaningful and trustworthy values.
arsenal.pickRiflePrecisionProjectButton: Pick from a Rifle Precision project…
arsenal.noRiflePrecisionProjectsHint: No Rifle Precision project has enough data yet for a usable precision figure.
arsenal.duplicateNameWarning: An entry with this name already exists in your Arsenal — saving will overwrite it.
arsenal.duplicateCartridgeNameWarning: Another cartridge on this rifle already has this name.
arsenal.confirmDeleteBulletWithCartridges: Delete "{{name}}" from your Arsenal? This will also delete {{count}} cartridge configuration(s) that use it.
arsenal.unsavedBadgeTitle: Not yet backed up to a file
arsenal.importConflictModeLabel: If a name already exists in your library
arsenal.importConflictModeHint: Choose how to handle items whose name matches something already in your library.
arsenal.importFileErrorInvalidFormat: That file doesn't look like an Arsenal export.

releaseHistory.title: Release history
releaseHistory.intro: What's changed in each release of this app.

entries.v219: Fix: moving target probability, flat zero. New: zero atmosphere, BC gain factor.
entries.v218: New: Backup & Sync cleans up after itself (unused photos, duplicate backup files, a persistent sync log) and lets you delete a device that is out of circulation, from any browser.
entries.v217: Fix: fixed broken output of chart SVG exports (Cd–Mach curve, Trajectory, Arsenal comparison, Labrabaco NG track chart).
entries.v216: Change: dropped the 'Live'/'Partial' status badges from tool listings (nav rail, category pages, Home) — nearly every tool is live now, so the badge was just noise; a not-yet-built tool still shows 'Planned'.
entries.v215: Change: renamed 'BC Labradar' to 'Labrabaco NG' (we did not have enough confusion as it were).
entries.v214: Fix: circular target zones (rings, gongs) now compute hit probability exactly via numerical integration, instead of approximating the circle as an equal-area square — that approximation could be badly wrong for a tight group aimed near a ring edge.
entries.v213: New: Hornady library data x-referenced with JBM's bullet length list. Length found for 69 entries, library updated (42 still missing).
entries.v211: New: user manual for the 'Backup & Sync' feature is now available.
entries.v210: New: this is major! Backup & Sync feature implemented, to replicate data between devices.
entries.v209: Change: bullet libraries now load as a single file per library instead of one file per bullet, making the offline cache more reliable on flaky connections.
entries.v208: New: as the bullets list grew, it's now sorted by caliber, then by library, then by manufacturer + name.
entries.v207: New: a bunch of new bullet libraries — Hornady, Berger, Sierra, and Lapua Cd-Mach curves reverse-engineered from Hornady's velocity tables. Plus, Berger bullets published BCs are now available as a library too.
entries.v206: New: detailed manual for the BC Labradar tool.
entries.v205: New: trajectory height, max point blank, and danger zone calculations.
entries.v204: New: zero with a different cartridge feature.
entries.v203: New: detailed Arsenal user manual, in-app, in all five languages.
entries.v202: Fix: corrected some terms in Russian.
entries.v201: New: Range Solver's photo target picker gets a Target label visibility setting (Settings) — always show labels, declutter them near the mouse pointer, or hide until tapped.
entries.v200: New: detailed user manual for the Rifle Precision Calculator tool. More of these are coming.
entries.v199: New: full-fledged markdown parser (Temml) integrated to display mathematical formulae in the upcoming extensions of the user manual. (Yes, some parts of the manual will be intense.) And a nice new codename.
entries.v198: New: Settings has a new Interface scale control (100-200%, in 25% steps) for a bigger, easier-to-read UI (thanks to Snuby642 for reporting).
entries.v197: Fix: every release was silently breaking offline mode — the browser's service worker update check doesn't notice a release that only bumps the version number, which could leave the offline cache stuck on the previous release (or empty). The app now detects real version changes itself and proactively rebuilds the service worker and cache instead of relying on the browser to notice.
entries.v196: Fix: the Rifle Precision Calculator's vertical zero offset was upside down — a group shooting low read as a positive number. Up is now positive everywhere, as on a turret; the CSV export's shot columns are renamed ShotRight/ShotUp to match.
entries.v195: Change: the Rifle Precision Calculator now draws every impact in the impact color picked in Settings, edge and all.
entries.v194: Fix: the Rifle precision calculator tool now understands archaic units.
entries.v193: New: added metadata for search engines, LLMs, and other bots.
entries.v192: Change: added link to the source code repository.
entries.v191: Fix: implemented offline cache auto-rebuild, to work around some browsers glitches when ServiceWorker could not be started (breaking offline functionality). Added an explicit 'rebuild cache' action to Troubleshooting pane.
entries.v190: Fix: set the correct step size for wind speed input in km/h (thanks to JerkyFreak for reporting)
entries.v189: Fix: the wind widget's speed value now renders centered in its dial hub, instead of overflowing off-center
entries.v188: Fix: minor fine-tuning of the built-in Swiss P library drag profiles
entries.v187: Fix: Hit Probability visual and functional fixes (thanks to Yuri Danilov for bug reports).
entries.v186: New: Hit Probability's impact-dot color is now a user setting — five choices, each drawn with a dark/white edge so it stays visible on any target (default: berry) — special delivery for Mr. Danilov. Change: USSR №4/№5/№8 targets' white non-scoring corners are now transparent.
entries.v185: New: muzzle velocity SD and own rifle precision (both optional) are now part of the Arsenal cartridge definition (and can be picked up automatically by Hit Probability). Rifle precision is now integrated with the Rifle Precision tool measurements, and can be picked directly. (Thanks to Yuri Danilov for the idea)
entries.v184: Fix: in desktop mode, the Guns tool's nav controls (Done/Manual entry/Arsenal) now stay in view while the Manual entry and Arsenal pages scroll, instead of scrolling out of sight with the page.
entries.v183: Fix: "Save to Arsenal" from the Cd-Mach curve tool now scrolls the Arsenal page to the bullet form it just opened, instead of leaving the page at the top of the list.
entries.v182: New: Swiss P bullet library, based on the vendor's velocity data. New cool release codename.
entries.v181: Fix: text fields and dropdowns (rifle/cartridge/bullet names, the cartridge picker, Range Solver's target picker, and more) had no color of their own and could render invisible dark-on-dark on Android browsers that auto-dark native form controls independently of this app's own theme — every field and dropdown now gets an explicit background/text color regardless of type (thanks to 6.5SH for the bug report).
entries.v180: Fix: Range Solver's clicks-output readout labeled itself with the rifle's own scope click unit (mrad/MOA) — since a click's actual size is arbitrary and can differ between elevation and windage, this misstated the value; it's now labeled "Clicks" instead.
entries.v179: New: IPSC Target and IPSC Mini Target (cardboard, three nested A/C/D scoring zones) added to Hit Probability, with a Major/Minor power-factor toggle for scoring.
entries.v178: Fix: pages could silently keep serving an old cached version even on a fresh visit — every request now forces a real network fetch instead of letting the browser's own HTTP cache quietly answer it from disk.
entries.v177: Fix: installed/home-screen apps on Android could get stuck on an old version indefinitely — the app now actively checks for updates on launch and whenever it returns to the foreground, instead of relying only on the browser's own update check.
entries.v176: Fix: on low-height mobile viewports, the fixed bottom tab bar could overlap the last portion of a page's content (e.g. the bottom of Hit Probability's Total Error chart) on devices with an on-screen navigation bar, since the space reserved for it didn't account for that bar's safe-area inset (thanks to 6.5SH for reporting).
entries.v175: Fix: input field and panel borders were barely visible in the dark theme, and high-contrast-light's borders fell short of its own high-contrast standard; both, plus a few marginal label and validation text colors, now meet accessible contrast levels (thanks to 6.5SH for reporting the issue).
entries.v174: Change: Hit Probability's simulation-parameter labels now show which statistical measure each figure represents (SD, R50, or median error).
entries.v173: New: IPSC popper targets (standard and mini) in Hit Probability. Gauss-Legendre hit prob calculations are now available under the hood for random-shaped symmetrical targets.
entries.v172: Fix: Hit Probability's target detail image briefly requested a nonexistent file when the default target was a user-sizeable one (Circle gong).
entries.v171: Change: in landscape mobile mode, the navigation bar now sits on the left edge (matching desktop's layout) instead of the right.
entries.v170: Fix: the active target's range value in Range Card's table could render smaller than the other rows' instead of larger.
entries.v169: New: Range Card view in Range Solver — all targets for a given location, on the same screen, with visual on-photo picker (thanks to ma smith for the idea).
entries.v168: New: user-sizeable circle and rectangle targets for Hit Probability (props to 6.5SH for the idea).
entries.v167: New: built-in unit conversion tool (again, 6.5SH’s idea, “for the full offline ‘Swiss Army Knife’ experience”). Check it out under “Analysis”.
entries.v166: New: RA4 (Subsonic rimfire) added as a standard drag model, for .22 LR and other rimfire loads (special delivery for 6.5SH). Off by default — enable it under Settings > Ballistic models.
entries.v165: New: a "Show Troubleshooting pane on Home page" setting (off by default, under Settings > General) — turn it on to see the Diagnostics info download on Home, without cluttering the About section for everyone else.
entries.v164: Fix: the service worker could silently fail to register on some page loads due to a timing race with the browser's load event — the likely root cause of the erratic offline/caching behavior reported over time. Diagnostics info now also logs the registration attempt itself, not just its outcome.
entries.v163: New: a "Troubleshooting" section on Home (under About) with a "Diagnostics info" download — a file with app version, cache/offline status, and storage info, useful when reporting a problem.
entries.v162: Bugfix: a single failed locale download could leave the whole app stuck on the loading screen forever, and a bullet/rifle/target that failed to load once could stay permanently broken for the rest of the session even after reconnecting. Both are fixed.
entries.v161: Bugfix: x-axis labels on the Trajectory chart and the Arsenal comparison chart could overlap each other when the window was narrow, or resized narrower. Labels are now thinned automatically to stay readable at any width.
entries.v160: Bugfix: the built-in bullet/rifle/target libraries could vanish entirely if just one of them failed to load, and reloading the app while offline could land on the browser's own "no internet" page instead of the app itself. Both are fixed.
entries.v159: Bugfix: the range solver's elevation/windage readout could look lopsided if only one side wrapped its sign onto a second line (narrow screens, or long mrad/MOA values) — they now wrap together. Also fixes a related glitch that made this trigger even when nothing had actually wrapped.
entries.v158: Bugfix: offline install could be silently killed entirely by a single flaky download during first-time setup; failed downloads are now retried before giving up, and one that still fails no longer takes the rest down with it.
entries.v157: Fix: renamed the 'icons' folder to 'app-icons' (and adjusted all references to it), to avoid a collision with Apache's default icons override on some hosts.
entries.v156: Bugfix: offline functionality (some tools failed to run offline, if never used online before).
entries.v155: New user setting: range solver output units, special delivery for our click-impaired friends.
entries.v154: The 'high speed low drag' range solver just got more awesomer — everything key is in a single pane now, no more clicking back and forth. Also, a version bump and a new release code name (because I thought of a cool one).
entries.v153: Feature to crop images on import. Increased image quality (resolution and lossy compression factor).
entries.v152: The THANKS page is no longer a stub.
entries.v151: New awesome wind input widget design.
entries.v150: A mess with two 7mm calibers sorted out — now properly separated into 6.8 and 7 proper. Props to ForgeValley for raising it.
entries.v149: Nice round range defaults for yards (when selected) in Trajectory and Hit Probability.
entries.v148: Icons and layout tweaks to improve PWA mode on iOS and Android.
entries.v147: Added a "loading" indicator on application start-up.
entries.v146: Engine upgrade to 4-DOF / MPM. Spin drift calculations implemented by McCoy's equations. McCoy's transverse moment of inertia constant (corresponding to .308 168gr SMK projectile) replaced by length-to-caliber-dependent function fit, calibrated with Lapua 6-DOF data.
entries.v145: Bugfix: fixed how the Range Solver's distance and wind speed inputs handle non-metric units — rounding and step size. (Props to 6.5SH.) Feature: added a "U/D, L/R" option for the Range Solver's output indicators (not translated).
entries.v144: The last of the tools has been ported to the new suite platform: meet the Rifle Precision Calculator (formerly known as Taran) – perhaps the most controversial, offensive, ego-shattering, pride-wounding, humiliating, demoralizing, and butthurt-inducing piece of software I've ever written. There's also automatic migration of Locations data from the old storage back-end to the new one, some UI polishing, and an update to the user manual reflecting everything that's happened since v136 (2.2). All this mandates a major version bump, and an awesome new version codename.
entries.v143: Implemented IndexedDB storage back-end, and migrated Locations data storage to it.
entries.v142: New unit setting – wind speed – separate from the general velocity, and used for all wind inputs across the project.
entries.v141: Range solver moved out to its own top-level navigation entry. Mobile presentation adjusted to accommodate one more icon.
entries.v140: Implemented a tool to convert multi-BC to custom curve (and to single optimal BC). Ever since Sierra realized we live in the third millennium, the tool is less useful than it used to be, but you never know who would want to be unique next.
entries.v139: Added a "Hornady reverse radar" built-in bullets library, with a few bullets I actually care for (more to come).
entries.v138: Unit-related UI fixes / accessibility features for our metric-impaired friends.
entries.v137: Bugfix: some UI elements ignored weird user unit preferences, and defaulted to metric.
entries.v136: Support of multiple built-in bullet libraries, individually switchable for display. Import of Lapua radar measured Cd-Mach curves as "Lapua Cd" lib. Minor UI enhancements.
entries.v135: Input validation / sanity checks implemented all over the app. Arsenal entry UI reworked to make it (hopefully) clearer, and (certainly) awesomer.
entries.v134: The Range Solver is final, with a beautiful (optional) feature to save target data for a location, and pick your targets directly from a photo taken from the shooter's position. Major polishing of mobile interface, to make portrait and landscape modes display correctly on various devices. All this mandates a major version bump, and an awesome new version codename.
entries.v133: Range Solver: a summary conditions bar was added above the elevation and windage readout, showing target range, wind, and atmosphere at a glance.
entries.v132: BC Tools is complete: BC Conversion now converts a ballistic coefficient between standard drag models at a chosen reference velocity, live as you type. BC Tools no longer shows as Partial.
entries.v131: Minor UI clarifications and bug fixes.
entries.v130: First public release. Since the last update: Labradar BC fitting now solves the whole velocity-vs-time window against the physics model directly, instead of a per-pair linear fit, paired with a tighter default de-noise threshold. UI improvements.
entries.v129: Added the Labradar tool to BC Tools: upload a Labradar chronograph export (a .zip of track files) to fit a BC per shot, with the same noise-cleaning approach as the original standalone tool, adjustable signal-quality and outlier filters, and a velocity-vs-time chart per track.
entries.v128: UI cosmetics: the wind-angle dial on Trajectory is now 1.75x larger, and it's centered together with its manual-degrees entry within the field.
entries.v127: Added six more standard drag models (G2, G5, G6, G8, GI, GS) alongside G1/G7, corrected G7's own table at high Mach numbers, and added a Settings toggle to show or hide individual models — G1 and G7 stay visible by default, the rest are opt-in.
entries.v126: Merged the BC Estimator, BC — Time of Flight, and BC — Labradar Track tools into one BC Tools page with Calculation, Conversion, and Labradar tabs — switch between a measured far velocity or a time-of-flight reading, and your entries now persist when you navigate away and back.
entries.v125: Fixed a bug where changing the comparison chart's max distance in Arsenal (or Trajectory) could blank the chart and leave the zoom sliders stuck on "NaN".
entries.v124: Cd-Mach Curve is live: paste a Doppler radar or chronograph distance/velocity table and back out the bullet's own drag curve, segment by segment. Chart it against G1/G7, export the tables, and save the result straight to Arsenal.
entries.v123: The Hit Probability tool is now a target-rich environment. Migrated all targets from legacy Plan 33 code, stand by for more scenarios.
entries.v122: Cosmetic changes / interface polishing for public release. Great thanks to S.E. for thorough review and feedback of v104, driving most changes implemented since then.
entries.v121: On mobile, Range Solver's Wind tab now sizes its direction dial to fit the screen and hides the manual degree entry (the dial itself stays fully operable, including by keyboard).
entries.v120: Trajectory calculations now interpolate between simulation steps with a quadratic (3-point) fit instead of linear, reducing the small residual error at in-between ranges.
entries.v119: Added a separate unit preference for rifling twist rate (mm or inches), independent of the sight-height/aim-offset unit choice.
entries.v116: Added bullet stability (Miller) and spin drift (Litz) calculations, removed the "example" rifles and bullets from the built-in library, gave every built-in rifle its rifling twist, and added release history with update notifications (can be turned off in Settings).
